claims.text: Immunosuppressants (glucocorticoids, azathioprine, mycophenolate, cyclosporine, tacrolimus) slow the dz but don't relieve Sx rapidly
claims.quote: Immunosuppressants (eg, glucocorticoids, azathioprine, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus) interrupt the autoimmune reaction and slow the disease course, but they do not relieve symptoms rapidly.

claims.text: Azathioprine may be as effective as glucocorticoids; benefit may take many months
claims.quote: Azathioprine 2.5 to 3.5 mg/kg orally once a day may be as effective as glucocorticoids, although significant benefit may not occur for many months.

claims.text: Myasthenic crisis: IVIG or plasma exchange
claims.quote: If patients have a myasthenic crisis, treat with IVIG or plasma exchange.

claims.text: Generalized MG, antibody-positive: AChR+ → efgartigimod, eculizumab, ravulizumab, zilucoplan; AChR+ or MuSK+ → rozanolixizumab, nipocalimab
claims.quote: Several medications are approved for the treatment of generalized myasthenia, including efgartigimod (anti-AChr antibody positive), rozanolixizumab (anti-AchR or anti-MuSK antibody positive), nipocalimab (anti-AchR or anti-MuSK antibody positive), eculizumab (anti-AChR antibody positive), ravulizumab (anti-AChR antibody positive), and zilucoplan (anti-AChR antibody positive).

claims.text: Complement inhibitors: meningococcal vaccination first (or prophylactic abx if started urgently)
claims.quote: Complement inhibitors require meningococcal vaccination prior to initiating treatment, or prophylactic antibiotics if treatment is started urgently.

claims.text: Cholinesterase-inhibitor abdominal cramps and diarrhea: oral atropine or propantheline
claims.quote: Anticholinesterase medications can cause abdominal cramps and diarrhea, which are treated with oral atropine or propantheline.
